study.title: Resting-State Functional Connectivity Patterns Predict Acupuncture Treatment Response in Primary Dysmenorrhea
study.study_design: Longitudinal randomized controlled trial with two parallel arms (real and sham acupuncture), with resting-state fMRI at baseline and post-treatment
study.blinding: All patients and study staff were blinded to the treatment groups. Only the acupuncturist was not blinded.
study.population: Women with primary dysmenorrhea recruited from advertisements and word of mouth
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) a regular menstrual cycle (27-32 days); (2) a history of PDM longer than 1 year; (3) no exogenous hormones or centrally acting medication in the last 6 months; (4) lower quadrant abdominal pain (including cramping, swelling, tingling, etc.) during menstruation in the last 6 months rated higher than 4 on a visual analog scale (VAS) (0 = not at all, 10 = the worst pain sensation); and (5) right-handedness, as confirmed by the Edinburgh Handedness Inventory
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) other chronic pain conditions, such as low back pain; (2) organic pelvic disease or abnormalities found in gynecological ultrasonography; (3) visceral pain and other neurology that may cause hyperalgesia; (4) a positive pregnancy test or plan for pregnancy; (5) a neurologic or psychiatric disorder history; and (6) any contraindication for MRI scanning

extraction_notes.note: No coordinate tables are reported. All neuroimaging results are reported as ROI-to-ROI functional connectivity edges without MNI coordinates. No peak or cluster-level coordinate data is available for extraction.
No expectancy or credibility measures were reported in the paper. No guessed allocation data was reported. Blinding success was not formally assessed beyond stating participants were blinded.
Adverse events are not mentioned or reported in the paper. It is unclear whether they were systematically assessed.
Trial registration number is not reported in the paper.
Post-treatment SAS and SDS values are not reported; only baseline values appear in Table 1. Whether these secondary outcomes showed significant changes after treatment is not reported.

Exact T values and p-values for individual FC edges in the paired t-tests and MANCOVA results are not reported in the text; only the direction of change and the figure are provided. Exact statistics for individual FC pairs (other than those in Table 2) are not available.

The paper states '8 paired FCs showed significant differences' in MANCOVA and lists: right aINS-bilateral S1, right dlPFC-bilateral S1, right dlPFC-left IPC, RVM-bilateral thalami, RVM-PAG. Counting these: right aINS-left S1, right aINS-right S1, right dlPFC-left S1, right dlPFC-right S1, right dlPFC-left IPC, RVM-left thalamus, RVM-right thalamus, RVM-PAG = 8 edges. Extraction follows this count.

Supplementary Figure S1 (real and sham acupuncture targets) and Supplementary Figure S2 (additional MANCOVA results) are referenced but not provided in the PDF. Some FC results may be only in supplements.

FC matrix patterns and FC change figures (Figure 3, Figure 4) display results visually. Statistical values for individual cells in the FC matrix are not tabulated in the text. Only the direction of change and narrative summary are provided.

The paper describes 'RVM-DMN (all four ROIs in the DMN)' as increased after real acupuncture, suggesting four separate edges (RVM-mPFC, RVM-PCC, RVM-left IPC, RVM-right IPC). These have been extracted as separate edges but individual statistics are not reported.

The number of ICs from GICA is stated as 'the median of the MDL over all subjects was 66,' and ten cortical ROIs were manually chosen. The exact ICA decomposition thresholds and IC selection criteria are not fully described in the methods.
Table 1 reports T and P values for group comparisons but uses 'T' for both independent t-tests and what appear to be two-sample t-statistics. These have been extracted as reported.
No information is provided about deqi or sensory responses using quantitative instruments (e.g., MASS, SACS). Only qualitative descriptions of intended deqi sensations are given.

The paper states that both groups received treatment 'once a day, there were 7 days in a session, and there were 3 sessions over 3 menstrual cycles.' Total number of needling sessions is thus 21, but this is inferred from the text, not stated as a single number.
